brain_mood.function: Your brain controls your thoughts, sleep, reflexes, and feelings.
brain_mood.space_effect: Isolation and schedule changes can disrupt sleep and increase stress [REF-01]. Fluid shifting to your head can also affect your vision and mental sharpness [REF-02].

heart.function: Your heart pumps blood to deliver oxygen and energy to your body.
heart.space_effect: Zero gravity makes your heart work less, which can reduce its size and strength over time [REF-03]. Returning to gravity can make you feel dizzy because your heart has to work harder to pump blood up to your head [REF-04].

lungs.function: Your lungs bring in oxygen and remove carbon dioxide.
lungs.space_effect: Dust, floating particles, and high cabin CO2 can irritate your breathing [REF-05]. Fluid shifts can also slightly change how air moves in your lungs [REF-06].

immune.function: Your immune system fights off germs and keeps you from getting sick.
immune.space_effect: Spaceflight stress, radiation, and altered sleep can weaken your immune system [REF-07]. This makes it easier for dormant viruses to wake up or for you to catch a cold [REF-08].

metabolism.function: Your metabolism turns food into energy and manages your body temperature.
metabolism.space_effect: Spaceflight changes how your body uses sugar and stores fat [REF-09]. You might lose your appetite, making it hard to maintain your body mass [REF-10].

bones_muscles.function: Your bones and muscles give you strength, structure, and the ability to move.
bones_muscles.space_effect: Without gravity loading your body, muscles shrink and bones lose density very quickly [REF-11]. Daily heavy exercise is required to prevent major bone and muscle loss [REF-12].

radiation.function: Your body's cells constantly repair themselves from daily wear and tear.
radiation.space_effect: Space radiation damages your DNA faster than your cells can fix it [REF-13]. High doses increase your lifetime risk of illness and can cause immediate fatigue or nausea [REF-14].
